title: Warehouse Restock Pairs
description_html:
Warehouse Restock Pairs

You manage inventory for a warehouse. You are given a list itemWeights representing the weight (in kg) of each box currently on a shelf, and an integer truckCapacity representing the exact weight a delivery truck can carry in a single trip.

You want to find the indices of the two boxes whose combined weight is exactly equal to truckCapacity, so both can be loaded together on one trip.

Return the two indices (0-based) as an array, in any order. You may assume exactly one valid pair exists for each input.

Example:
Input: itemWeights = [4, 7, 11, 2], truckCapacity = 6
Output: [0, 3]  (because itemWeights[0] + itemWeights[3] = 4 + 2 = 6)
constraints:
- 2 <= itemWeights.length <= 10^4
- -10^9 <= itemWeights[i] <= 10^9
- -10^9 <= truckCapacity <= 10^9
- Exactly one valid pair of indices exists
- Time limit: aim for O(n) or O(n log n) solution

title: Server Session Merge
description_html:
Server Session Merge

A monitoring tool logs user sessions on a backend server. Each session is recorded as [startMinute, endMinute], representing when a session began and ended (in minutes since server start). Sessions may overlap or touch each other, in which case they should be treated as a single continuous session for billing purposes.

Given a list of session intervals (not necessarily sorted), merge all overlapping or touching intervals and return the resulting list of merged sessions, sorted by start time.

Example:
Input: sessions = [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]
Output: [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]
constraints:
- 1 <= sessions.length <= 10^4
- sessions[i].length == 2
- 0 <= startMinute <= endMinute <= 10^6
- Intervals that merely touch (e.g. [1,3] and [3,5]) must be merged into one
- Expected complexity: O(n log n)

title: Balanced Config Blocks
description_html:
Balanced Config Blocks

You are building a validator for a configuration file format that uses three kinds of bracket pairs to define nested blocks: (), {} and [].

Given a string config containing only these six bracket characters, determine whether every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket of the same type, and whether brackets are properly nested (i.e. the most recently opened block must be the first one closed).

Return true if the configuration string is valid, otherwise false.

Example:
Input: config = "{[()()]}"
Output: true

Input: config = "{[(])}"
Output: false
constraints:
- 0 <= config.length <= 10^4
- config consists only of the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[', ']'
- An empty string is considered valid

title: Design an LFU-Style Cache Evictor
description_html:
Design an LFU-Style Cache Evictor

You are designing a small in-memory cache module for a backend service. The cache has a fixed positive capacity. Implement a class FrequencyCache that supports the following operations, each in O(1) average time:

  • get(key) - Return the value of the key if it exists in the cache, otherwise return -1. Accessing a key counts as one use.
  • put(key, value) - Insert or update the value of the key. If inserting a new key causes the cache to exceed its capacity, evict the least frequently used key. If there is a tie in usage frequency, evict the least recently used key among those tied.

Both get and successful put operations should increase the usage count of that key by 1.

Example:
Operations: FrequencyCache(2), put(1,10), put(2,20), get(1), put(3,30), get(2), get(3)
Expected results: [null, null, 10, null, -1, 30]
(Explanation: capacity is 2. After put(1,10) and put(2,20), get(1) makes key 1 used twice. put(3,30) must evict the least frequently used key among {1,2}; key 2 has frequency 1 so it is evicted. get(2) then returns -1 since it was evicted. get(3) returns 30.)
constraints:
- 1 <= capacity <= 10^4
- 0 <= key, value <= 10^9
- At most 2 * 10^5 calls total will be made to get and put
- Aim for O(1) average time complexity per operation
